title: Put it together: build an example end to end
idea: Take a tiny task, name input and output, write the full example, and connect it to the print code you'd use — all the pieces of this unit at once.

exercises.prompt: Task: 'show the word Hello'. What's the very first thinking step?
options: Name the input and the output
exercises.explanation: Start by naming input and output. That's the Understand/Example thinking before any typing.

exercises.prompt: Same task. What is the expected output?
exercises.explanation: The task asks for Hello, so the hand-worked output is Hello — exactly.

exercises.prompt: Which print line would produce the output Hello? (review from Unit 1)
exercises.explanation: print("Hello") — text in matching quotes, inside brackets. The example (Hello) tells us this is the right code.

exercises.prompt: Put the whole mini-rhythm in order for this task.
blocks: Write the example output by hand
Check the real output against the example
exercises.explanation: Understand, example, code, check. The example in step 2 is what step 4 compares against.

exercises.prompt: Task: 'show Hi, then Bye'. What's the full expected output?
exercises.explanation: Two lines, in order: Hi then Bye. You worked the multi-line example by hand.

exercises.prompt: Which code produces that output? Put the print lines in order.
exercises.explanation: print("Hi") first, then print("Bye") — matching the example lines Hi then Bye. (Review of Unit 3's several prints.)

exercises.prompt: Which of these did you practice in this unit? (pick all)
options: Naming the input of a task
Writing the expected output by hand
Using it as a check later
exercises.explanation: All four — name I/O, work the example, catch bad examples, and use the example to check. That's the E of the rhythm.

exercises.prompt: The output you wrote by hand is what you'll compare the real output to.
exercises.explanation: Yes — the hand-worked example is your check value. This ties the whole unit together.

exercises.prompt: Task: 'show the number 7'. The example says 7; the program prints 7. Pass or fail?
options: Pass — real output matches the example
exercises.explanation: The screen shows 7 and the example expected 7. They match, so it passes. You used the example as your check.

exercises.prompt: You can now do which thing, that you couldn't before this unit?
options: Write a concrete input->output example for a task before coding
exercises.explanation: That's the Out goal of Unit 4: hand-work a concrete example first — the E of the rhythm. Great progress!
